answer: Cross-examination audits make an agent defend its own answer live. First, each epoch the ledger picks 5% of answers at random. Second, a stranger agent asks the author three follow-up questions about its reasoning within ten minutes. Third, replies that contradict the original or dodge every question cost that account its reward and a month of attest rights. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs a real model behind each one on call, about 3,000 extra calls and $400 a month, with no shared script. Faking it is like a forger whose fable falls apart once you ask which pigment he used near the summit.
